sections.label: HCSA phased implementation timeline
sections.summary: The Act is implemented in three phases: laboratory, radiological, ambulance and medical transport services in 2022, hospital, medical and dental services in mid-2023, and nursing home services at end-2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Since 1980, the healthcare landscape in Singapore had undergone many significant changes and it was timely in 2020 to update the regulatory framework to become services-based and premises-neutral, to ensure that our regulatory approach remains relevant and flexible.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The Act is being implemented progressively with licensees coming onboard HCSA in three phases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: We started with laboratory, radiological, ambulance and medical transport services in Phase 1 in January 2022 and will be progressing to hospital, medical and dental services in Phase 2 in mid-2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Lastly, we will onboard the nursing home services in Phase 3, planned for the end of 2023.

sections.label: Removing 14-day licence notice
sections.summary: Clause 11 amends section 14 to remove the 14-day notice period for modifying licence conditions applying to a class of licensees where harm to patient safety or public health is immediate or imminent.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: To prepare for future emergencies, clause 11 will amend section 14 to remove the 14-day notice period for any modification of licence condition that applies to a class of licensees, where there is immediate or imminent harm to patient safety or public health.

sections.label: Approval for Specified Services
sections.summary: New section 9A requires licensees to seek approval for providing any Specified Service, in addition to the existing licensing regime.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: In addition to the existing licensing regime for licensable healthcare services, the new section 9A will require licensees to seek approval for the provision of any Specified Service.

sections.label: CGO appointment approval framework
sections.summary: Clause 17 amends section 24 to replace the existing notification regime for appointing a CGO with an approval framework.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Clause 17 will amend section 24 to replace the existing notification regime for the appointment of a CGO with an approval framework.

sections.label: Specialty names in licensee branding
sections.summary: Clause 19 amends section 29 to prohibit licensees from using a specialty name in their names or logos in any language if no practitioner actively practises that specialty under the service.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Clause 19 will amend section 29 to prohibit licensees from using a specialty name in their names or logos – in any language – if there is no practitioner actively practising the said specialty under the auspices of that licensable healthcare service.

sections.label: Advertising rules under HCSA
sections.summary: Some advertising requirements for non-licensable healthcare services will be regulated under the HCSA regime, and relevant provisions in MASA will be repealed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: To streamline the regulatory framework for healthcare service advertising, some advertising requirements for non-licensable healthcare services will now be regulated under the HCSA regime, and the relevant provisions in the Medicines (Advertisement and Sale) Act 1955 (MASA) will be repealed.

sections.label: Doctor title disclaimer requirement
sections.summary: New section 31B requires non-registered healthcare professionals using the title "Doctor" in healthcare advertising to state their qualifications and a disclaimer.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: To protect consumers from being misled into thinking that such persons are registered medical or dental practitioners when they are not, the new section 31B inserted by Clause 22 will require any person who is not a registered healthcare professional to state their specific qualifications and a disclaimer that their qualification is not a medical or dental qualification should they wish to use the title of "Doctor", or any derivative in any language, in healthcare service advertising.

sections.label: Implementation timing and licence framework
sections.summary: The Amendments are intended for mid-2023 implementation with two exceptions, and the Bill introduces an approval framework for healthcare service licences.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: If passed, we intend to implement the Amendments in mid-2023, together with the second phase of the implementation of this Act, with two exceptions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Second, the restriction on individuals employed or engaged will be implemented at end of 2023 when the screening process for the prospective employees would be operationalised.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: With that, Mr Speaker, I beg to move.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This Bill also introduces an approval framework for licences to providers of healthcare services which will strengthen and refine the regulation of healthcare services.

sections.label: Licence condition modification without notice
sections.summary: Section 14 will be amended to allow a licence condition to be modified without the 14-day notice period to prevent or mitigate immediate or imminent harm to patient safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Section 14 will be amended to clarify that a licence condition can be modified without the 14-day notice period if it is necessary to prevent or mitigate immediate or imminent harm to patient safety.

sections.label: Doctor title advertising restrictions
sections.summary: New section 31B restricts use of the title "Doctor" in healthcare service advertising, requiring disclaimers where it describes someone who is not a medical practitioner or dentist.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 31B will restrict the use of the title "Doctor" in the advertising of a healthcare service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Where the title is used to describe someone who is not a medical practitioner or dentist, the advertisement must provide appropriate disclaimers, such as by stating that the title is not a medical or dental qualification.

sections.label: Workers' Party support for Bill
sections.summary: The Workers' Party supports the Bill, stating that all these are unobjectionable.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: All these are unobjectionable and for this reason, the Workers' Party supports the Bill.

sections.label: Definition of service facilities refined
sections.summary: Clauses 2 and 3 of the Bill and sections 3 and 8 of the original Act refine the definition of service facilities to include remote healthcare provisions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Clauses 2 and 3 of the Bill as well as sections 3 and 8 of the original Act, refine the definition of service facilities so as to weave in the possibility of remote healthcare provisions such as via the Internet or telephone.

sections.label: Advanced practice nurses licensing
sections.summary: Advanced practice nurses date back to 2006, and only 57 are currently licensed to prescribe medicine.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Advanced practice nurses, senior nurses who possess advanced training and can take on some roles in diagnosis and treatment, date back to only 2006, and currently, only 57 are licensed to prescribe medicine.

sections.label: Healthcare staffing and physician numbers
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked about filling healthcare niches, with 2016 data showing 2.3 physicians per 1,000 people and plans to increase prescribing advanced practice nurses to 700.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: What steps has the Ministry undertaken to fill the niches that currently exists in our healthcare service providers?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The latest available data, which applies to 2016, for example, indicates that Singapore has 2.3 physicians per 1,000 people, a little higher than the world average of 1.7, but substantially below the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) average of 3.8.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is also pertinent in the light of how our current slate of medical professionals are reportedly burning out, a bipartisan concern that has been raised in this House by, among others, my hon friend Ms He Ting Ru as well as the hon member who just spoke, Mr Louis Ng.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I understand that there are plans to increase the number of advanced practice nurses able to prescribe medication to 700.

sections.label: Registrable medical qualifications list
sections.summary: The registrable medical qualifications list numbers about 100, with few recent additions, and France has one university listed versus Australia's eight.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The list of registrable medical qualifications only numbers to 100, while a few additions have been made in recent years, these are only a small handful.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is hard to conceive of how a country, like France, with a population and medical school count, almost three times that of Australia, has only one lonely university on the list, versus Australia's eight.

sections.label: SMA and SMC involvement
sections.summary: The speaker was involved via the Singapore Medical Association and Singapore Medical Council and asks how many doctors responded.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I was involved via the Singapore Medical Association (SMA) as well as the Singapore Medical Council (SMC).

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, I would like to know how many doctors actually responded.

sections.label: SMC, SMA roles and HCSA scope
sections.summary: The SMC versus SMA role should be ingrained in medical students, and the expanded HCSA scope is welcomed with a request to include beauty and wellness services.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In addition, the role of SMC versus SMA should be ingrained into medical students, so that as doctors progress in their careers, they value how a professional body can effectively do group representations with MOH in policy engagements.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I welcome the expanded scope of HCSA to include complementary and alternative medicine.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But I still ask for consideration to include beauty and wellness services as well, I remain concerned over misleading claims.

sections.label: Delayed breast cancer diagnosis
sections.summary: While that may be true for most women, a few have breast cancer and delayed seeing a doctor until months later.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While that may be true for most women, a few actually have a breast cancer and they delayed seeing a doctor until months later.

sections.label: Director-General of Health approval powers
sections.summary: New sections 11(A) to 11(D) give the Director-General of Health power to approve premises, conveyances or service delivery modes for licensable healthcare services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: New sections 11(A), 11(B), 11(C), 11(D) give wide-ranging power and responsibilities to the Director-General of Health, currently called the Director of Medical Services, in granting an approval for any permanent premises, conveyance or other services' delivery mode, which I understand, can include telehealth, for licensable healthcare services of a licensee.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Under section 3 of HCSA, health services definition is very broad and can range from, I quote: "assessment, diagnosis, treatment, prevention or elevation of any ailment, a condition, disability, disease, disorder or any injury affecting any part of the human body or mind, nursing or rehabilitation care of an individual suffering from an ailment, a condition, disability, disorder or an injury, assessment of the health of an individual." While I understand that this new section 11 is an extension to the replacement to the previous Private Hospitals and Medical Clinics Act that is more premise-based, to a more service-based legislation through HCSA first enacted amidst the thick of COVID-19 pandemic in January 2020, I would like to ask how these new sections would be judiciously administered, with a balance between safeguarding patient safety and not stifling the development of new and innovative healthcare services that can benefit Singaporeans?

sections.label: Advertisement prohibition and licensee exception
sections.summary: New section 31(A) prohibits advertisements inducing people to seek treatment, but exempts advertisements of licensable healthcare services by licensees or their authorised persons.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The new section 31(A) prohibits the advertisement of any skill or service relating to the treatment of any ailment, disease or condition and so on, affecting the human body such that it induces a person to seek the advice of, or treatment from the advertiser or the person being advertised.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, this prohibition does not apply in relations to an advertisement of a licensable healthcare service by a licensee, or a person acting on the authority of a licensee.

sections.label: Public education and clause 19
sections.summary: A clarification is sought on how the Ministry plans to enhance public education regarding clause 19, which amends section 19 of the Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, Mr Speaker, Sir, I would like to seek clarifications on how the Ministry plans to enhance public education, particularly with regards to clause 19 of the Bill which seeks to amend section 19 of the Act.

sections.label: Clarification on clause 11
sections.summary: A clarification and safeguard is sought concerning clause 11 of the Bill, which amends section 14 of the Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Second, Mr Speaker, Sir, there is a need for clarification and safeguard concerning clause 11 of the Bill that amends section 14 of the Act.

sections.label: Regulation of community services
sections.summary: Greater clarity is sought on the regulation of community services, such as community screening.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Third, Mr Speaker, there is a need for greater clarity on the regulation of community services, such as community screening.

sections.label: Complementary and alternative medicine scope
sections.summary: A question is asked on whether complementary and alternative medicine will be considered under the scope of the HCSA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Fourth, Mr Speaker, Sir, will complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) be considered under the scope of the HCSA?

sections.label: Chiropractic services regulation calls
sections.summary: Chiropractic services are not recognised in Singapore, and since 2018 there have been calls for the industry to be regulated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Despite not being recognised in Singapore, chiropractic services have been discussed in articles by local mainstream and online publications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: From 2018, there have also been calls for the chiropractic industry to be regulated, even from within the industry itself.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry share an update on its assessment of risks to patient safety and the need for possible regulation?

sections.label: Community health-screening services review
sections.summary: The Ministry is reviewing whether to regulate community health-screening services that may involve invasive procedures not provided by a medical practitioner or dentist.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: One concrete example, we are reviewing whether to regulate community health-screening services that may involve invasive procedures, such as the drawing of blood, but which may not be provided by a medical practitioner or dentist.

sections.label: Retaining restricted business names
sections.summary: Existing licensees and businesses with restricted terms "National" or "Singapore" can retain their names unless the business name or licensee changes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Mr Yip had asked whether existing licensees and businesses that contain the restricted terms "National" or "Singapore" will be allowed to retain their names.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: I mentioned that they can continue to use these terms unless there is a change in the business name or a change in the licensee.

sections.label: Specialist requirement for licensees
sections.summary: Licensees may keep existing names, but regulatory requirements may be imposed to employ or engage the relevant specialist if they provide specialty services.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: They may continue to use those names that they already have.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: But if they provide or purport to provide services within that specialty, we may impose regulatory requirements on such licensees to employ or engage the relevant specialist.

sections.label: Advertising and complaint investigations
sections.summary: The Ministry will not prevent all advertising but will investigate complaints case-by-case, suggesting reports of non-licensed providers using visual imagery.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, we do need to be quite careful, not to prevent all advertising.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We will investigate complaints, however, on a case-by-case basis, and the examples that he cited, if there is a non-licensed provider, or someone purporting to treat when they should not be, and doing so through the use of visual imagery, we would suggest that these cases are reported.

sections.label: Co-location of non-licensable services
sections.summary: A prescribed list of services that can be co-located without prior approval includes TCM acupuncture and services by registered allied health professionals such as physiotherapists.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Ms Ng Ling Ling had some questions on the co-location of non-licensable healthcare services, such as Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) practitioners together with licensable healthcare services.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We have prescribed a list of services that can be co-located without needing to seek prior approval and this includes TCM acupuncture services and services provided by registered allied health professionals, such as physiotherapists.

sections.label: Advertisement compliance for co-located services
sections.summary: The HCSA licensee is responsible for ensuring the entire advertisement complies with the Healthcare Services (Advertisement) Regulations when it covers both licensable and co-located non-licensable services.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Where an advertisement covers both the licensable healthcare service and the co-located non-licensable service, it is the HCSA licensee that is responsible for ensuring compliance with the Healthcare Services (Advertisement) Regulations for the entire advertisement.

sections.label: Prohibition on treating and diagnosing
sections.summary: They are prohibited from purporting to treat and diagnose medical conditions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: What they are prohibited from is purporting to treat and diagnose medical conditions.

sections.label: Overseas online healthcare information
sections.summary: The Bill cannot regulate what people access through the Internet or information from overseas healthcare providers, but the public will be educated to be discerning.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Indeed, the point he brought up around international providers around the virtual tele-consultations is important.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We cannot regulate what people has access to through the Internet, but we do want to educate members of the public to be discerning about where they get their healthcare information from.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: If they do get information online from healthcare providers overseas, that is not something that this Bill is going to be able to regulate.

sections.label: Vaccination subsidies and GP flexibility
sections.summary: Vaccination subsidies are beyond the Bill's scope, but the Bill provides flexibility for GPs to perform vaccinations in community centres and other locations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: If the issue is the subsidies for vaccination, that is beyond the scope of this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: If the question is about could GPs perform vaccinations in the community centres and other locations, it is precisely this sort of flexibility that this Bill now provides.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The specifics would depend on which GP, which vaccination and which community centre.
